races.name: Ct Electrical Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: A Mayo Breeze
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 120 and returns from a lengthy 261-day absence, so fitness is the central question; a natural hold-up horse that the field's depth of closers pushes toward a midfield berth, limiting its ability to race in its preferred patient style.

runners_data.name: Boo Radley
runners_data.note: Mullins sends this four-year-old out with a hood for the first time since a 276-day break, signalling a horse that may be keen — Brian Hayes will look to settle it quietly and deliver a late run on going similar to its two prior starts.

runners_data.name: Gethegoodtimesroll
runners_data.note: A veteran of 8-year-old maidens, this horse shows a pattern of fading finishes and has pulled up twice recently; the field's density of hold-up types means it cannot realistically operate from its preferred rear position, compounding an already weak profile.

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: Unknown style horse who ran just nine days ago (hg:p, cheekpieces retained) and has been competitive without winning over today's trip on similar ground — the freshness angle is a concern but a willingness to travel forward could carve out an uncontested lead.

runners_data.name: Returning Officer
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends Jack Kennedy to Sligo with this lightly-exposed six-year-old whose three hurdle runs have all been over trips around today's distance on Good or Yielding — the trainer's 7/54 in 14 days is a strong yard stat and Kennedy's positional intelligence is the key asset here.

runners_data.name: Rosenborg
runners_data.note: Rothwell's five-year-old has finished well off the pace in both hurdle starts on Good ground and has shown little sign of getting competitive; 33 days since last run and nothing in the form to suggest it can improve enough to factor.

runners_data.name: Tommy Go Maith
runners_data.note: Has pulled up twice from three hurdle starts and not run for 154 days (with a fall flag at 94 days), making this a significant fitness and jumping confidence concern on a sharp track; the fade pattern is a further deterrent.

runners_data.name: Brother Hollie
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a tongue-tie (hg:t) who has finished mid-division in five hurdle starts, never troubling the leaders — displaced from its natural rear position by the field's composition, it would need to race positively against its instincts.

runners_data.name: Nile Star
runners_data.note: Shows a fade pattern alongside three hurdle runs finishing tenth, tenth, twelfth, and thirteenth — the only positive run was a fifth on Good to Firm 9 days ago, but its natural closing style is compromised by the field dynamics pushing it toward midfield.

runners_data.name: Tribal
runners_data.note: Three hurdle starts all finishing seventh or worse, including a 10th over 22f on Good — a true hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield forces it out of role, and the fade pattern across all three runs offers no confidence.

runners_data.name: Middlethird Marvel
runners_data.note: Returned after a 286-day break with a consistent series of midfield finishes (6th, 11th, 12th, 13th) all on Good or similar; Slevin rides but the fade flag and unbroken win/place duck across four comparable runs makes this hard to recommend on shape grounds.

runners_data.name: Unknown Fortune
runners_data.note: Lightly raced eight-year-old (just two hurdle runs) with an unknown tactical profile — a 6th and 12th on similar ground suggest moderate ability, but the unknown style at least leaves open the possibility of racing prominently into an uncontested lead.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner maiden hurdle on Good to Firm ground at Sligo, the field is dominated by hold-up and unknown-style horses, meaning the early tempo is likely to be modest and uncontested rather than genuinely strong. Hey Sir, Returning Officer, and Unknown Fortune carry unknown pace profiles and may drift forward simply by default, but none has a established front-running pattern — the absence of a true pace-setter points strongly toward a race that crawls before erupting into a sprint finish over the final two hurdles. The firm ground amplifies this dynamic: Sligo's tight track will compress the field further, making tactical position at the second-last hurdle the decisive factor. A Mayo Breeze, Nile Star, Brother Hollie, Tribal, and Gethegoodtimesroll are all natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate that many genuine closers at the rear — of those, A Mayo Breeze (highest OR at 120, Jack Kennedy-calibre jockey in Philip Donovan) and Boo Radley (Mullins-trained, hg:h) are best-placed to actually secure a workable position tracking the pace. This race shape favours horses who can settle in a handy midfield position and accelerate sharply off a slow pace — prominent or tracking mid-division types who avoid the traffic nightmare that a bunched sprint finish creates for true hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the race crawls at a steady tempo and erupts into a sprint over the final two flights, with the field compressing and tactical position at the second-last proving decisive.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo on Good to Firm ground at Sligo produces a bunched field that turns the race into a sharp-ground flat sprint, favouring horses with pace and clean jumping. Returning Officer (Kennedy, Elliott) and Hey Sir, both unknown-style types who may naturally travel prominently, are ideally positioned to kick off the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mullins Handicap Guile
scenarios.trigger: If Boo Radley travels smoothly in rear-midfield under Brian Hayes and delivers a well-timed run from off the pace to exploit a compressed sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Mullins sends out this four-year-old with a hood (hg:h), suggesting a horse that needs restraining — Hayes will aim to produce him late into a race that sets up perfectly for a well-schooled, sharp traveller. The Good to Firm ground suits a horse whose two prior runs came on similar conditions, and a sprint finish rewards class over stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unknown-style horses — Hey Sir or Unknown Fortune — stamps authority early and sets a controlled solo lead that the hold-up dominated field cannot adequately challenge.
scenarios.body: With no dedicated front-runner in the field, a horse willing to go forward and jump fluently could dictate terms unchallenged and turn it into a test of jumping accuracy rather than a sprint. Hey Sir (hg:p, recent run 9 days ago, has shown mid-field form but could exploit the vacuum) or Unknown Fortune could steal a march on a hold-up-heavy field slow to organise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the sprint finish creates a wall of horses and one genuine hold-up type threads through late on the flat run-in to snatch the race.
scenarios.body: This requires a clean passage through a compressed, tightly-packed finish — a low-probability ask given how many true hold-up types are mapped ahead of their natural position and will be racing out of role. A Mayo Breeze (highest OR 120, 261 days off, unknown freshness) is best credentialled of the redistributed closers if the gaps appear at the last.

watchPoints.text: Watch Returning Officer in the market — Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy at 7/54 in 14 days on a horse unexposed over this trip on Good ground is a powerful combination if it drifts forward naturally in the absence of a true front-runner.

Monitor Boo Radley's jumping and early behaviour — the hood is new and the 276-day break means Brian Hayes may need to work hard to settle it, but if it travels fluently it could arrive dangerously late in a sprint finish.

Hey Sir ran just nine days ago and carries cheekpieces — if it takes up a front position unchallenged on a track where no other horse is willing to go forward, the price could be wrong and it becomes the controlling factor for all scenarios.

With five true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield, watch for a congested run to the second-last hurdle — horses drawn or ridden wide (Brother Hollie, Tribal, Nile Star) may be blocked when the sprint begins and their chances evaporate regardless of ability.

The Good to Firm ground is confirmed across all seven races at Sligo today — any horse showing hesitation at the first flight or jumping errors early (Tommy Go Maith, Gethegoodtimesroll given recent pull-ups) should be dismissed immediately as the sharp track punishes jumping errors severely.

races.name: Durkin Bros. Electrical Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beat The Devil
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 4yo with prominent/lead profile is the lone front-runner here and controls the early tempo; the [STYLE_FIT] tag slightly tempers confidence as this position is not fully natural, but 28 days since last run on matching Good ground is acceptable.

runners_data.name: Bobby Kirova
runners_data.note: Has finished tailed off in heavy company and carries a notable fade-in-finish flag; the 30-day freshener from a fall comes into a race where similar going previously produced only a remote 13th, and stamina beyond 10f is unproven.

runners_data.name: Casheldale Lass
runners_data.note: Andrew Kinirons-trained hold-up mare with genuine form credentials including two wins in 11 starts on Good ground; came back from a fall 18 days ago and 7 career runs at this trip distance give her strong profile credentials for this specific test.

runners_data.name: Emmamia
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — Mark McNiff runner with no public form record and going listed as UNKNOWN; lightly-raced flag means any rating or style assessment is speculative, making her a pure wildcard in market terms.

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: Long 98-day absence for Eamonn O'Connell and a true hold-up horse by nature — though the map shows him in midfield, that reflects a crowded rear rather than his natural ride; his best form is on AW at 8f, so the hurdles trip and surface are both a stretch.

runners_data.name: Hygge
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott 4yo with a consistent placing record (four thirds and a win visible across five runs), all on Good ground; the 98-day gap (including a fall) is a concern, but class of trainer, solid sim-going profile of 4/6 runs, and prominent style all align with this race shape.

runners_data.name: I'm All In
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning from 209 days off carrying two unseated-rider runs and a pulled-up; the fade-in-finish tag combined with youth and a long absence make this a very difficult proposition in a 14-runner maiden.

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Raced just 6 days ago and brings a consistent placing profile (three seconds and a third from eight sim-going runs); prominent style suits the expected race shape and Gordon Elliott's yard is in strong form with 5 wins from 37 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Megaball
runners_data.note: Francis Casey newcomer with zero prior form and no trainer strike-rate data — impossible to assess on pace or going grounds, so purely a candidate for the wildcard scenario.

runners_data.name: Noble Rocco
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott 4yo with a sole run on Good — a seventh over 16f — giving very limited evidence; the high OR of 120 assigned suggests connections see ability, and the Elliott stable is in form, but one run tells us little about style or trip suitability.

runners_data.name: Pebble Island
runners_data.note: John McConnell's hold-up type has placed twice from 15 sim-going runs including a second on Good over 12f; returned 8 days ago and has previously unseated, so jumping fluency is a mild concern over hurdles on this quick surface.

runners_data.name: Sylvie Power
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle newcomer with no public form and going listed as UNKNOWN — impossible to categorise by style or confidence, a blank-sheet wildcard entry.

runners_data.name: The Chancie Grey
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's lightly-raced 4yo has one run to his name (fifth over 16f on Good) with 37 days between starts; insufficient evidence to project a reliable shape or going read, though the trainer has 2 from 26 in recent fortnight.

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's prominent-style 4yo returned 8 days ago and has a decent sim-going profile of 9/15 runs with three placings; the 'O' (pulled up) in recent form is a concern, but he races off a mark of 107 and a track-style that suits competitive positioning here.

races.paceDynamic: Beat The Devil is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner maiden hurdle and, with no other horse genuinely looking to dominate from the front, should be able to bowl along at a sustainable Good to Firm gallop without any serious pressure through the early stages. Hygge, Manoir De Mirande, and Whats New are all prominent-style runners who will look to track closely, creating a compact, moderately-paced contest rather than a searching test of stamina. The field does hold more hold-up types than can genuinely operate from the rear — Georg Zhukov is a true hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield because the rear positions are saturated, meaning his natural race-riding is compromised. On this shape — one front-runner, a sustainable tempo, Good to Firm ground at Sligo — the race strongly favours closers who can travel prominently and produce a clean late challenge, rewarding horses with a proven prominent or tracking profile who stay organised over 2m1½f on quick ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Beat The Devil controls a fair but uncontested gallop and the race is truly run to suit those travelling in the first three on the bridle.
scenarios.body: Beat The Devil sets a comfortable tempo and the race develops into a test of cruising speed and jumping fluency through the straight; horses prominent from flag to finish have the clearest route to the line with no late-run traffic to navigate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Beat The Devil gets a completely uncontested lead and converts it into a front-running success on the quick ground.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to close the gap early, Beat The Devil builds a comfortable lead and the Good to Firm surface suits a rolling gallop that grinds out the finish; prominent-to-lead types who stay on resolutely are the main beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to compromise the prominent brigade and genuine finishers from off the pace come through.
scenarios.body: A truly run race from the front opens the door for horses who have been ridden patiently, arriving with a sustained run in the closing stages; Casheldale Lass and Pebble Island, with hold-up form credentials, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Upsets Market
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced or debut runners — Emmamia, Megaball, or Sylvie Power — possesses hidden ability that emerges on first serious public test.
scenarios.body: Unraced or lightly exposed horses can land maiden hurdles when the pace is fair and competition is modest, as a field full of maiden-race regulars can be vulnerable to a well-schooled newcomer; the Good to Firm ground and the manageable trip are permissive conditions for a fresh horse to shine.

watchPoints.text: Beat The Devil sets the sole front-running platform — if he gets a completely uncontested lead over the first mile, the pace map collapses for every hold-up runner and prominence from the front becomes decisive; watch the early stages closely for whether any rider challenges him.

Hygge's 98-day absence (including a fall) for Gordon Elliott is a significant fitness unknown — if he travels kindly but weakens after the last, prominent-to-lead horses like Manoir De Mirande and Whats New inherit the frame positions.

Georg Zhukov's natural hold-up style is compromised by the saturated rear of this field — if jockey cannot find clear daylight in the closing stages from a midfield position, his finishing effort will be further blunted than his raw form suggests.

Good to Firm going is confirmed across all Sligo races today — horses with a fade-in-finish flag (Bobby Kirova, I'm All In) are at further risk on quick ground that often stretches stamina reserves late in 2m1½f maiden hurdles.

Three complete newcomers (Emmamia, Megaball, Sylvie Power) plus Noble Rocco (one run) represent over a quarter of the field with near-zero form data — in a maiden hurdle on this scale, a well-schooled debutant trained by a powerful yard can spring a surprise if the pace is moderate.

races.name: Racing Tv Irish Ebf Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kenisa Sport
runners_data.note: Front-runner on a retrieval mission after 290 days off; two wins from similar going and an 0.93 style-fit flag suggest she may be drawn wider than ideal but the lack of lead competition is her biggest asset.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare whose best form has come on Good ground at around 2m-2m1f; only 12 days since last run and a 7lb claimer up, but the steady pace this race is likely to produce may not extract her best finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: Most recent run was a win on Good ground over 2m; true hold-up type who benefits from a proper gallop, and the headgear (blinkers) sharpens her early sections without moving her forward positionally.

runners_data.name: Our Lucky Lady
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight runs on similar going and a natural prominent style that should see her slot in just behind the leader; hood on, 72-day break is a minor query, but trainer Fahey has had recent runners.

runners_data.name: Radar Ahead
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was last out only 8 days ago and showed a willingness to press on; distance is on the short side based on recent 3m-plus assignments, but the fast ground and sharp Sligo track may neutralise that concern.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: Tongue tie on; placed twice at around 2m-2m1f on Good ground and a natural front-rank type who should get close to the pace without leading; OR of 103 gives her a weight advantage and Enright is a strong claimer.

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Returned after a 444-day absence (22-day freshener flag) and ran twice at 10f on the Flat before this; a genuine front-runner whose style-fit flag and redistribution mean she is unlikely to travel where she wants — long absence adds further risk.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: Five runs on Good going from eight this season and consistent placed form at this sort of trip; her natural prominent style has been pushed back on the map due to a crowded front end, and the style-fit flag tempers her chance in a shape where she cannot get her position.

runners_data.name: Doyen Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two recent second-place finishes, though both came on Heavy ground at Hereford; the switch to Good to Firm at Sligo is an untested surface shift and the 3lb claimer Shane O'Callaghan reduces the weight burden marginally.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Returned three wins from thirteen runs on similar going but all over shorter trips of 12-14 furlongs; redistributed from her natural prominent position, and the step up to 2m1½f on fast ground asks a question her form does not yet answer.

races.paceDynamic: Kenisa Sport is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she can dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on this Good to Firm ground at Sligo. The field does contain more prominent-minded types than can physically secure those early positions — Albatala, Crystabel, and Steps In The Sand are all natural trackers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning there will be quiet jostling behind Kenisa Sport rather than a true pace battle. Our Lucky Lady and Radar Ahead should press from close range, creating a small front group but one unlikely to generate a truly searching tempo over 2m1½f on fast ground. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace — strongly favours horses who travel comfortably in the first two or three and can produce a clean jump-to-jump round; confirmed prominent types who can get on terms early hold a decisive positional edge over true hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kenisa Sport Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kenisa Sport gets away cleanly and settles into an uncontested rhythm with no rival willing to go with her, she controls tempo and pinches a winning advantage.
scenarios.body: She has proven front-running form at this sort of track and trip, winning twice from five runs on similar going, and a comfortable lead over 2m1½f on Good to Firm ground maximises her stamina and jumping rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Our Lucky Lady or Radar Ahead push Kenisa Sport harder than expected, the race develops into a two-way contest between the leading group with a fast-finishing close-up rival intervening.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace benefits a horse who has been tracking just off the front and can produce a decisive jump at the last; Our Lucky Lady's three wins on similar going make her well-suited to this minor-pressure shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front group sets a genuinely brisk tempo and ties itself up in the straight, a true hold-up runner who has been travelling well in behind can finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Splashing Out and Beauforts Storm are the most credible hold-up types in the field with genuine closing form, though the anticipated steady pace makes it less likely they get the searching gallop they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Find Position
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses shuffled back — Albatala, Crystabel, Steps In The Sand — manage to push forward and secure a better position than the map suggests, the race becomes more congested up front.
scenarios.body: This scenario demands those mares race out of their mapped role and is therefore the least probable, though Crystabel's recent placed form at similar distances gives her a residual live chance should chaos create a gap.

watchPoints.text: Kenisa Sport jumps away cleanly — if she clears the first hurdle in front and settles, she immediately becomes the race-shaper and every scenario funnels off her early sectional.

Albatala and Steps In The Sand — both natural prominent types pushed into midfield — watch for crowding and interference from the third hurdle if they attempt to move up from an unnatural starting position.

Splashing Out's headgear (blinkers) combined with a hold-up style means she could take a wider line entering the back straight; jockey Peter Smithers on a 7lb claim needs to manage her racing room carefully.

Going read is repeated as Good to Firm across all races — monitor any on-course ground inspection closer to post time, as any softening would particularly benefit Beauforts Storm and Doyen Magic whose best form has come on an easier surface.
Radar Ahead ran only 8 days ago and switches from a much longer trip; watch how she travels after the third hurdle — if she tightens up early it signals the quick turnaround has left its mark.

races.name: Foley's Bar & Off Licence Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Wolf Prince
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse whose course-and-distance form on Good ground reads encouragingly (1W4P on similar), but the 807-day absence is a serious flag and the 7lb claimer Conor Smithers rides for a trainer with a modest 14-day record; needs everything to fall right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Stormbreaker
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from 446 days off for James Fanshawe — the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/3 adds to the concern, and his hurdle form string of 62000 shows a horse that has declined sharply; the uncontested lead is his only realistic weapon.

runners_data.name: One Last Tango
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who comes here 198 days fresh with a recent second on Good ground in his form, but the U (unseated) on latest visible start and a pair of unfurnished question marks in the history string mean jumping reliability is uncertain on quick ground.

runners_data.name: Bridgehead
runners_data.note: Most course-realistic prominent mover in the field — Noel Meade's charge ran 28 days ago, has 14 runs on similar going (1W6P), and his latest form shows a second just two runs ago; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a useful advantage at the weights.

runners_data.name: Cappucino
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two wins on comparable going (2W2P in nine similar-ground runs) who ran creditably 41 days ago; the blinkers are already fitted, removing a potential headgear variable, and Richard Deegan is a reliable partner for this profile.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old hold-up type sporting a hood, last seen finishing third 48 days ago over further; his form at 2m1½f is untested in recent runs and the step back in trip combined with quick ground could see him outpaced when the pace lifts late.

runners_data.name: Tell Us This
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse with a recent win at this trip (1/16f/GOO) and solid recent third on Good; Andrew McNamara's yard is 2/8 in the last 14 days and the tongue-strap is already established — well-placed tactically and profile fits the pace map best.

runners_data.name: Listentillitellyea
runners_data.note: Ageing prominent type (10 years old) whose form string of /F-769 reads uninspiringly, with a fall the only notable highlight recently; 29 days since last run is fine but Harry Sexton's 7lb claim cannot disguise the lack of competitive form.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner freshest in the field (just 10 days since last start), Gordon Elliott's yard is 2/11 in the 14-day window, and form shows three seconds at this trip on Good ground (1W4P); the hood is already a known quantity and Kevin Sexton takes the ride — profile suits if the pace is truly honest.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural position has been displaced by superior speed in this field — the 5lb claim from Eoghan Finegan is an asset, but McCourt's yard is 0/7 in 14 days and the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 reflects a horse that is unlikely to get his preferred berth from stall.

runners_data.name: Mary's Pride
runners_data.note: Form shows a second and a third on Good ground (1W4P) and she ran just 35 days ago for Edward Cawley, but her true hold-up preference cannot be expressed here — the field's prominent types will push her further back than ideal, limiting her chance unless the race falls apart.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: On a career-low mark of OR 90 and shown in eight of nine recent runs on Good or similar going, but consistently finishing mid-to-rear (best recent position: 4th); Thomas O'Connor's 7lb claim helps at the weights, yet the horse's natural hold-up role is crowded out by true closers who outrank him.

races.paceDynamic: Stormbreaker is the one confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Sligo, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any serious challenger for the lead — this is a single-paced, uncontested pace scenario. Behind him, Tell Us This, Bridgehead, and Dairy Force are the genuine prominent types who will press for the positions just off the pace, while the hold-up horses — Wolf Prince, Cappucino, Grange Walk, and One Last Tango — will be anchored in rear. The field contains more speed than the map can accommodate: Maxwell Smart and Mary's Pride are natural prominent or hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their preferred position and may be squeezed into an unnatural role. With a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a measured clip on quick ground, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel within striking range and produce a sustained finish — pure closers are disadvantaged by the lack of a truly pressured pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stormbreaker Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Stormbreaker is allowed to dictate alone at a comfortable clip, the race develops as a one-pace affair with minimal mid-race pressure.
scenarios.body: Stormbreaker lobsters along in front without being challenged, keeping the gallop honest enough that the race is run at his tempo, and horses that travel prominently behind him get the best of the fractions. Tell Us This and Bridgehead, sitting just off the pace with proven form on similar going, are ideally placed to challenge from the second-last flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Favourite
scenarios.trigger: If Stormbreaker's long absence (446 days) tells in the final half-mile and he fades, the horses racing prominently in his wake inherit the prize.
scenarios.body: Bridgehead's recent return (28 days ago, form showing a latest second) and Tell Us This's win at this trip on Good ground combine to make them the chief beneficiaries of a late fade from the leader. Dairy Force, freshest of the group (ran 10 days ago) and consistently placed on Good ground, makes the frame.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses rapidly in the straight and the front end burns out, genuine closers arriving late from off the bridle can overhaul the field.
scenarios.body: Wolf Prince, a proven winner at this course on similar going and returned after a long absence with a bold showing, and Cappucino, who has placed twice on comparable going, would be the primary beneficiaries of a truly strong gallop that punishes front-runners. However, this scenario is partly dependent on hold-up horses that have been redistributed into midfield and may not be in their natural position, moderately limiting its likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the tightly-packed prominent group fractures the race shape — crowding, interference at hurdles, or a pace collapse — an unexpected winner emerges from the pack.
scenarios.body: With twelve runners, amateur and conditional jockeys prominent in the booking, and several style-redistributed horses out of position, the risk of traffic issues or a ragged pace is real. Mary's Pride or Phoenix Arizona, shuffled back from their preferred positions, could benefit if the race fragments and gaps appear.

watchPoints.text: Stormbreaker's 446-day absence combined with a trainer at 0/3 in 14 days makes his ability to sustain that front-running role over 2m1½f on Good to Firm very questionable — watch for him stopping sharply from the second-last.

With five conditional or amateur jockeys in a 12-runner hurdle race on quick ground, jumping errors and traffic interference are elevated risks — especially at the early hurdles where the field will be bunching behind Stormbreaker.

Maxwell Smart, Mary's Pride, and Phoenix Arizona are all likely to be out of their preferred positions from an early stage — any one of them could make an aggressive move to reclaim ground, causing disruption to the horses around them in the first mile.

Tell Us This carries a tongue-strap and has already won at this trip on Good ground; his market move at declaration time will be informative given the pace scenario suits his profile as well as any runner in the field.

Bridgehead's trainer Noel Meade has saddled 22 runners in 14 days (2 winners) — a high-volume yard that targets competitive handicaps; with the horse having run just 28 days ago and showing a recent second, stable confidence is worth monitoring in the ring.

races.name: Kilcawley Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Go To Town
runners_data.note: Unclassified style makes pace positioning unpredictable; seven similar-going runs yield zero wins and zero places, which is a damaging stat on this fast surface over 2m4f with Ross O'Sullivan's yard running at 2/17 in the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Cherry Red
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with a fade warning, but the one recent win came over 18f on Good — Ben Harvey rides, and if he can manoeuvre closer than normal in a redistributed field, a second placed run looks more likely than a win.

runners_data.name: Lilac Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a strong record in similar going (14/15 sim-going runs) and four places in five recent starts; the 7lb claimer Alan King keeps the weight low, but she will need things to go her way positionally having been placed in midfield rather than at the rear.

runners_data.name: Papagei
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who maps to midfield by necessity rather than choice; best going figures come on Good (4/24f most recently), and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim helps, but 60 days since last run is worth monitoring alongside only six similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the race's pace anchor; tongue-tie applied, and while style-fit is flagged (0.93) suggesting she rarely leads, she is the only horse likely to do so here, making her tactical significance far greater than her handicap mark of OR 94 implies.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: Prominent type with tongue-tie and a placed run over 17f on Good — handlers John McConnell and Alex Harvey know this trip suits, though 44-day absence and a record of eight similar-going runs without a win tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: Unclassified style and only eight days since last run; form figures include a fall and a pulled-up, and sim-going record of 8/11 with zero wins suggests he is unlikely to threaten despite Andrew Slattery's strong 14-day strike rate of 3/27.

runners_data.name: Saint Peregrine
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three places from 15 similar-going runs but a troubled recent record including falls and pulled-ups; J J Slevin is a significant rider booking, though the 13th-place finishes in recent Goodwood-ground hurdles suggest he needs things to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at OR 79-80 over 20f on Good and Soft make this prominent racer one of the most interesting profile fits; Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim helps, and P J Rothwell's yard is in form (3/28), making this a natural beneficiary of a Poppycon-led pace.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with a fade warning who has been mapped to midfield against her natural style; eight runs without placing in similar going and an OR of 84 make this a horse to oppose rather than side with in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Tellmemamema
runners_data.note: Another genuine closer carrying a fade flag who lands in midfield by redistribution; five recent runs on similar going with a best of 4th tells its own story, and the style displacement reduces her chance materially in what shapes up as a front-runner's race.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: 112 days off the track is a significant concern for this hold-up horse who maps to midfield rather than her natural rear position; I Madden has no 14-day runners recorded, and the form figures include a fall and a pulled-up.

runners_data.name: Mr Erwitt
runners_data.note: 267 days absent — a striking layoff — and a hold-up style that has been redirected to midfield; fade warning applies, V T O'Brien has only two runners in the 14-day window, and the long break allied to a poor sim-going record of 5/5 with zero placings makes this a very difficult profile.

runners_data.name: Finnicky Filly
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has finished 2nd twice in recent form over similar trips on Good ground; John Patrick Ryan's yard is 2/28, and while OR 78 represents the bottom of the weights, her consistency (all finishes between 2nd and 6th recently) makes her a quiet player in Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Sekifi
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie, fade warning, and a hold-up style that cannot be accommodated at the rear — bumped to midfield — with a sim-going record of 9/14 runs without a win; Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim is some compensation but this profile is poorly served by the projected race shape.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Hanlon-trained hold-up horse with three places from 15 similar-going outings and a headgear flag; mapped to midfield rather than the rear because of redistribution, and the 0.92 style-fit discount reflects that she cannot settle as naturally as her form demands.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with one win and six places from 15 similar-going runs — the best placed profile in the entire field alongside Larkins Lane; no jockey listed yet, Norman Lee's yard has gone 0/7 in 14 days, but the form (3rd, 2nd in recent 22f Good runs) fits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Cornaroya Rocco
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Hanlon yard (also trains Mother Ship) with a pulled-up on most recent start and a sim-going record of 5/6 runs without a win; the 2m4f trip is an extension from recent 2m outings, and form figures of P65-4P offer little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Poppycon is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4f on Good to Firm ground at Sligo, and with no rival likely to seriously press for the early lead, she can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front. The prominent types — Fine Print, Larkins Lane, Ladiam, and Finnicky Filly — will track in her wake, forming a compact lead group, while the bulk of the field clusters in midfield given the redistribution of multiple genuine hold-up horses who cannot all secure their natural rear position. This field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Mother Ship, Frontier Rose, Tellmemamema, Dream Shaper, Mr Erwitt, and Sekifi are all true closers who will be shuffled into midfield positions against their nature, meaning late-running scenarios are structurally weakened. A sustainable, honest gallop set by one uncontested front-runner on fast ground over an extended trip strongly favours horses racing prominently or from a close-tracking position, with the prominent and tracking profiles best placed to capitalise if the pace is judged well from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poppycon Leads, Prominent Track
scenarios.trigger: If Poppycon dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent chasers track efficiently throughout.
scenarios.body: Poppycon controls the pace on fast ground without pressure, and the horses sitting closest to her — Fine Print, Larkins Lane, Ladiam — are ideally positioned to challenge approaching the last with energy in reserve. On a tight, undulating Sligo track over 2m4f, the race regularly falls to those who travel well up with the pace rather than needing a sustained run from off it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Poppycon goes too fast early and burns out in the straight, opening the door for a close tracker to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A front-runner that has gone clear without cover can sometimes overcook the fractions on Good to Firm ground at a sharp course like Sligo, leaving the door ajar for the horse travelling best just behind the leader. Lilac Lady and Cherry Red, though natural hold-up types, have enough positional awareness and recent placed form to capitalise if they can travel closer than usual in this redistributed field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pace group tie each other up in a bunched finish and a horse from mid-division finds a run on the inside or outer.
scenarios.body: Sligo's undulating track can create gaps in the straight when a big field spreads out, and a horse tracking in midfield with a strong finishing position could benefit from a fortuitous passage. Tellmemamema and Papagei, though mapped to midfield rather than their truest position, have the ground preference and trip experience to be dangerous if the race develops with late gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Denied Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady throughout and the race is won entirely within the front four, leaving held-up horses with no room to land a blow.
scenarios.body: With so many genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield, they face compounding disadvantages — wrong position, no cover, and a pace that doesn't stress those ahead. Frontier Rose, Mother Ship, and Sekifi all carry fade warnings and poor positional profiles for this shape, meaning the field effectively runs as a front-runners-and-trackers affair from start to finish.

watchPoints.text: Larkins Lane and Ladiam are the two prominent runners whose recent form and sim-going profiles most align with a Poppycon-led controlled gallop — watch whether either can track the leader throughout and challenge from the second-last.

Poppycon's style-fit flag (0.93) means she is not a habitual front-runner — watch the early stages to see if she actually commits to the lead or if another runner (Fine Print, Finnicky Filly) moves past her to set the pace, which would change the shape materially.

The sheer volume of redistributed hold-up types (Mother Ship, Frontier Rose, Tellmemamema, Dream Shaper, Mr Erwitt, Sekifi) crowding midfield creates a traffic-management risk in the straight — watch for interference or horses checked when gaps don't appear.

Cherry Red and Lilac Lady both carry fade warnings but have recent placed form on similar ground — if either travels unexpectedly close to the pace in the early stages due to the bunched midfield, their chance upgrades sharply in Scenario B.

Mr Erwitt's 267-day absence is the most extreme layoff flag in the race; watch for betting market moves on this runner as any significant support would suggest connections have the horse ready despite the long break.

races.name: Sligo Park Hotel Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kalanisi Flash
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner here; recent course form includes a win over 22f on Good and form figures suggest it handles this type of trip — cheekpieces fitted and the combination of Dylan Kidd (7lb claimer) and John McConnell is live; racing in its natural role at the head of affairs, this is the key pace-setting asset of the entire race.|

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Noel Meade with a consistent record on Good ground but a worrying habit of fading in the finish; the form string of 9969-6 over shorter trips than today's 3m1½f is not encouraging, and the step up to this marathon trip looks like it may expose that stamina weakness.|

runners_data.name: Streets Of Doyen
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old veteran who holds course and distance form on Good ground; hold-up style suits a race that develops late, but the age profile and a recent pulled-up run over this sort of trip are reasons to temper expectations despite the solid historical going record.|

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: A prominent racer whose best win came over 26f on Good ground — today's trip suits — but a 181-day absence (returning after a fall) is a major flag; the 7lb claimer Alan King takes the ride and the form figures suggest it can handle this going if fit.|

runners_data.name: Evans Secret
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe in the saddle is an upgrade; this horse has won and placed repeatedly on Good ground over similar trips and races prominently — form of 1-2 in last two completed runs gives it genuine claims in a race shape that suits front-rank types.|

runners_data.name: Justatan
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins-trained hold-up horse returning after 168 days off; the heavy reliance on Flat-track Haydock-style going and a sim-going record of just 1 run from 5 on comparable surfaces is a significant concern at this trip today.|

runners_data.name: Sphagnum
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins on Good ground and a recent second over 26f on Good — the profile fits today's race shape well; the 7lb claimer J P Sampson takes the ride and the blinkers suggest connections want it switched on from the front.|

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Only 10 days since last run but an excellent sim-going record of 14 from 15 runs on comparable ground; placed at 2 and 3 in recent starts, this prominent racer handles trips around today's distance and should be competitive if the pace suits.|

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Sam Curling who placed third last time and has decent Good-ground form; the step up to 3m1½f is uncertain given all five recent runs have been shorter, but Philip Enright is a capable handler of these long-trip handicaps.|

runners_data.name: Kazbek
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey horse returning after 173 days — a lengthy absence that is concerning over this trip; a hold-up profile with limited evidence on Good ground (7 from 11 comparable runs) and all recent starts shorter than today's distance.|

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old who has been placed repeatedly on Good ground and won over 26f; the prominent style suits this pace shape and the recent fifth suggests the legs are still there, though John McConnell saddles both this and Kalanisi Flash, creating a mild team dynamic.|

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placing record on Good ground but all recent runs over shorter trips than today's 3m1½f; the 3lb claimer Shane O'Callaghan takes the ride and the lack of demonstrated stamina at this trip is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Joe's Turn
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer with two wins at 24-26f on Good ground and a strong prominent profile — the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects congestion at the front, not its natural style, and if it can slot into a forward position it becomes a live contender.|

runners_data.name: Ballagh Star
runners_data.note: Carries wins over 26f on Good ground and is a natural front-rank type; pushed to a midfield slot purely because of the volume of prominent horses in this field, not because of style, and the recent poor figures (P-0P) on softer surfaces cloud confidence on quicker ground today.|

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Recent form of 4-1-2 in last three completed starts on Good ground with wins over 25-26f — exactly this trip profile; a natural prominent racer whose map position understates its forward inclination, and Conor Stone-Walsh is an able handler who could get it into a front position.|

runners_data.name: Strong Contender

runners_data.name: Back The West
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old without a jockey listed in the data — that alone is a flag; form figures of PP on last two runs and a return from 52 days off make this a difficult case, and being a true prominent type squeezed into midfield only makes the task harder.|

races.paceDynamic: Kalanisi Flash is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, with no identified rival willing or able to push the pace from the front, should be able to dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 3m1½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Sligo. That uncontested lead is significant: on a flat, tight track like Sligo where front-runners can control tempo without burning energy, a horse allowed to bowl along in front at its own rhythm is difficult to peg back, particularly at this trip. The prominent-positioned types — Evans Secret, Sphagnum, Cornmarket, Tango Theatre, Smallcraftwarning — will track Kalanisi Flash and are best placed to capitalise if it weakens, while the hold-up brigade face a genuine challenge if the pace is modest and the race doesn't truly develop until the final circuit. This shape strongly favours prominent racers or horses that can quicken from just off a lone leader, as the steady early tempo will compress the field and make it very hard for true hold-up horses to find sufficient momentum late. The field carries far more prominent types than the map can accommodate: Joe's Turn, Le Grand Vert, Ballagh Star and Back The West are genuine front-rank horses forced into midfield slots on the map, and of these Le Grand Vert and Joe's Turn — both with strong prominent profiles and recent evidence of handling this going — are most likely to actually secure forward positions in the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kalanisi Flash Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kalanisi Flash is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a true but sustainable gallop that the hold-up horses cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: Kalanisi Flash dictates from the front on a track where lone leaders have a strong record, and the modest pace never truly stretches the field enough for closers to generate a winning run from the rear; the prominent types just behind benefit most if Kalanisi Flash tires late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kalanisi Flash sets a pace that is just fast enough to stretch the true hold-up horses but slow enough to leave prominent stalkers fresh for a home-turn challenge.
scenarios.body: Evans Secret, Sphagnum or Tango Theatre track the leader at close range and pick off Kalanisi Flash from the second-last hurdle, with their good going form and prominent profiles ideally suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the modest gallop set by Kalanisi Flash causes a bunched, tactical race and the field quickens collectively off a slow pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse with a sharp change of gear who has been tracking the pace — or one of the redistributed prominent types that manages to secure a forward position — delivers a late burst that catches a stopping Kalanisi Flash; Le Grand Vert, racing in a natural forward berth if it gets there, is the most credible beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong over 3m1½f on Good to Firm ground and the prominent types are all spent entering the final flight.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up horse such as Streets Of Doyen or Je Suis finds a late run through a tiring field, though this shape is the least likely given the controlled pace profile and the redistribution of several hold-up types whose stamina reserves may not be as deep as their map position implies.

watchPoints.text: Le Grand Vert has won and placed over 25-26f on Good ground in three of its last five starts and is a natural prominent racer who may force its way forward despite the crowded map — if it gets its position early, it becomes the single biggest threat to Kalanisi Flash.

Kalanisi Flash carries 168lbs and is ridden by a 7lb claimer returning after 74 days off — if the weight or the layoff tells in the closing stages, the race opens dramatically for the prominent trackers immediately behind.

With Joe's Turn, Le Grand Vert, Ballagh Star and Back The West all being natural front-runners redistributed to midfield, watch the first few flights carefully — a scrimmage for early position in a 17-runner field on this trip could see one of them force the early pace and change the race shape entirely.

Evans Secret with Darragh O'Keeffe is a notable jockey booking upgrade — this horse's 1-2 in its last two completed runs on Good ground over the right trip gives it strong credentials if it can travel prominently and save ground on Sligo's tight circuit.

Tango Theatre and Kalanisi Flash share the same trainer (John McConnell) — watch for any signs of a team plan, as Tango Theatre's prominent style could be used to set a pace that suits a stablemate or, conversely, the yard may be running both on their merits in an open handicap.
